title: Multi-agent rooms: turn-taking, governed delegation, agent-to-agent messages and background child work
summary: Let several agents live in one room and cooperate: a room coordinator fans out per-member turn requests (nonce, deadline, parent/root ids, outcome sent|pass|skipped|timeout|cancelled), a hop limit and loop detector (shadow first), and an agent-to-agent message contract with typed delivery outcomes. A delegate must re-resolve its own authority through Control, and the whole chain renders as one collapsed unit with an openable transcript. Child sessions carry space_id and audience.
whyItMatters: Humans plus several agents working in the same room is the core of the Space vision and the main gap relative to Grok Bot. Verevon's Control model (agents as their own subjects) is a better base for this than any reference, but today only one agent can be addressed per message and delegation is unbuilt.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (turn protocol); qm (orchestrator spine, subagent inheritance)
others: buzz (failure mode without a breaker)
slack (agent messaging docs)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Multi-agent turn-taking 2 of 5 (differentiator); agent-to-agent messaging 3 of 5 (common); subagents/swarms 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grok Bot coordinator fans out RequestMemberTurn{nonce, member, peers, new_messages, is_winding_down, deadline_ms, parent_request_id, root_parent_request_id}; members answer with outcome SENT|PASS|SKIPPED|TIMEOUT|CANCELLED; idempotency by nonce; hop limit via root-id depth; wind-down mode; loop detector off|shadow|on; UI shows each member's reading/typing/working phase. Agent messages: SendAgentMessage{from,to,message_id,text,reply_to} with outcomes FORBIDDEN|TARGET_NOT_FOUND|DUPLICATE, a collapsed 'messaged N agents' summary with openable transcript and a separate cost flow. QM spine: the coordinator cannot run tools, posts an early ack, delegates to child sessions (inherit caller scope+audience, durable mailbox that is data and never human authorization, tree caps, cycle checks) and is re-woken on completion.

verevon.constraints: Delegation is a side effect, so it can live only in execution-core's governed loop, never model-gateway's plain chat loop. The room composer never requests the agentic feature, so approval_mode auto is inert, and flipping it would hand the room agent execution-core's whole capability surface (browser, sandbox, registered capabilities): a narrow delegate_to_agent capability must exist first. Plane rules: execution-core has no network path to the gateway and must not call Convex (no cross-plane DB access); Control is reachable through the user_core_client precedent. ZDR: a ZDR run registers no child run, lineage or stored answer, so the collapsed chain and loop detection cannot rely on durable lineage for ZDR; peer content is untrusted data.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Stage it as SPACE_AGENT_SCOPE_PLAN already decides: (1) UI-2c narrow slice with a delegate_to_agent capability in execution-core, same room, one hop, human present, re-entering a new internal non-streaming gateway endpoint under the original human's session bearer and the existing persona pipeline, plus a collapsed card in SpaceRoomTimeline; (2) multi-mention fan-out in the gateway; (3) only then a coordinator with the nonce/deadline/outcome protocol and shadow loop detection. verevon.effortNote: Kept XL: the plan calls even the narrow slice multi-service and multi-session; the narrow UI-2c slice alone is L and the coordinator and turn protocol add to it.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap statement is accurate but the approach conflicts with the recorded UI-2c design (gateway callback with the human bearer, no Convex call from Rust) and assumes an Application event feed that does not exist; it should be restated as a staged build starting from the narrow slice.

title: Typed cards and agent input requests (forms and secret drop)
summary: Define a small Verevon card schema (sections, buttons, select, fields, chart, link, with a required plain-text fallback) that agents emit as typed tool results and rooms render natively, with actions round-tripping as typed run signals. Build the first card type as request_input: an agent tool that pauses the run, shows a form (choices, multi-step, custom answer, dismiss) and resumes on submit, where secure fields post straight to the Control credential broker and only an opaque handle enters the run.
whyItMatters: Structured input makes multi-human rooms readable (who answered what) and replaces long prose with compact actionable UI. Keeping secrets out of chat is mandatory for ZDR and for agents that sign in to services for a person. Both are visible quality jumps for agent messages.

others: grokbot
slack
teams
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Forms and secret capture: 2 of 5 (differentiator); cards/blocks: 2 of 5 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm's secret drop mints a one-time URL (7-day TTL) via mint/peek/redeem with take-on-redeem; the value goes to the person's keychain with an optional grant to the conversation and the transcript records only that a secret was provided. Grok Bot's request_input tool {fields[], secure, multi_step} creates a pending widget in the thread; Respond/Submit/Dismiss resume the run with a typed message. Slack Block Kit is the best-specified card schema (server-validated, action_id/value round-trips, required top-level text); Teams Adaptive Cards add charts and dynamic search.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Agent output renders Markdown, code and charts and there is a built-in approval card (owner-only decide, reconcile-on-error), but there is no general typed card schema with actions and no forms: agents can only ask in prose. Tool-call/plan cards and chat artifacts are absent in rooms. The credential broker for secret fields (S3.4) is planned only. The AG-UI stream accepts up to 32 caller-declared client tools (spot-check), which may carry the pause/resume round trip, but whether a client result resumes a Space run is unverified.

approachOriginal: Frontend Plane: card schema aligned with AG-UI generative-UI events, validated server-side in the gateway, rendered by the room timeline; start with buttons, select, fields, chart and link. Model Plane: request_input tool with a pause/resume contract that reuses approval continuation (or the AG-UI client-tool result path after verifying it resumes a Space run); card actions return as typed run signals through the gateway with a per-action authority check. Secret fields post directly to the Control credential broker (S3.4) and return an opaque handle; only the handle enters the run, transcript, logs and snapshots. Show the requesting agent's identity and destination on every form.
planeOwner: Model Plane (request_input and resume); Frontend Plane (card schema, renderer); Control Plane (credential broker)
risks: Phishing-style forms driven by injected prompts; card actions are an injection path and need server-side validation plus per-action authority; secrets must never reach transcript, logs, snapshots or the model.

verevon.exactGap: Rooms render user turns as plain text and assistant turns as Markdown (with chart fences) plus one built-in approval card (SpaceApprovalPanel, decided only by the run owner); there is no typed card schema, no request_input tool, no form and no card-action round trip, and no credential broker or secret-drop code exists in apps/Control Plane (S3.4 is plan-only). Agents ask today by ending the turn with a prose question (execution-core agent.rs SNIPPET_USER_SUPPLIED_ARGS). The AG-UI client-tool path cannot carry a pause/resume (caller-declared tools are only offered to the model, an unresolvable name returns an error to the loop) and approval-gated resume is itself quarantined pending a descriptor-backed dispatcher.

verevon.constraints: Runs are owner-bound, so only the member who started the run can answer a request (a second member answering needs an explicit delegation design). Approval-gated resume is quarantined (http_routes.rs:1555-1579, approvals.rs:254-272), so request_input cannot reuse approval continuation today. S3.4 explicitly says to reuse existing secret stores and not to add a QM-style keychain, which conflicts with the item's 'secret drop to a credential broker'. ZDR runs are persistence-free: answers and any continuation descriptor must not be stored for ZDR threads (continuation_gate already blocks resume under ZDR). Card actions must be validated server-side in the gateway under a Control decision; the browser never sends authority. The room composer rides the native chat stream, not AG-UI.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into two slices. (1) Cards: extend the existing shared/chat-nodes union with form/choice/link nodes and render them in SpaceRoomTimeline instead of inventing a new schema; validate server-side in the gateway. (2) request_input as an end-turn tool: the tool result carries a typed form node, the submit posts a normal Space append (a typed user turn) under the existing append decision and starts a new run, so no run pause/resume is needed and the quarantined approval continuation is avoided; true pause/resume waits for the descriptor-backed dispatcher. Defer secure fields until S3.4 lands and route them to an existing secret store (no new keychain); drop 'secret drop' from this item. Do not depend on the AG-UI client-tool path.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as a whole. The cards slice is M (reuse chat-nodes); request_input as end-turn plus typed reply is M-L; a true pause/resume variant would be XL and is blocked on the continuation dispatcher.
verevon.verdictReason: Not shipped (only the approval card exists), but the item's mechanism assumes approval continuation and AG-UI client tools that cannot resume a Space run, and its secret-drop half contradicts S3.4's 'no keychain' decision. Reword to reuse chat-nodes, use end-turn plus typed reply, and defer secure fields.

title: Agent operations: per-room and per-agent cost and budgets, admin allow/block, answer-quality surface, and room-behaviour evals
summary: Attribute usage to Space and agent binding by flow (chat, scheduled, agent-to-agent, browser, computer) in cost-core, add a per-Space allowance with warnings and a hard stop plus a room spend panel, and let admins allow or block agent definitions with a reason shown to users. On the answer itself add an AI label, citation chips and the thumbs-plus-reason feedback that /chat already has, a closed vocabulary of typed turn failures, and a room-behaviour eval suite that replays scripted multi-person scenarios against the gateway and Model Plane.
whyItMatters: Per-agent and per-room cost is table-stakes in four of five references, and it is the safeguard that makes multi-agent rooms, browsers and computers affordable to ship. Admins need to govern which agents may exist, and a room-behaviour eval is how Buzz keeps agents from becoming noisy or silent regressions.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (cost by flow and bot, hard limits); teams (AI label, citations, admin allow/block); buzz (room-behaviour evals)
others: qm (rolling-window admission check, multiplayer scenarios on real Slack)
slack
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Cost and usage attribution 4 of 5 (table-stakes); AI labelling/citations/feedback 3 of 5 (common); admin governance 2 of 5; turn resilience and typed failures 2 of 5; room-behaviour evals 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Buzz per-turn usage record {turn usage, cumulative, null for unknown, deltaReliable, session/turn seq}; Grok Bot series centsByFlow and centsByBotId, hard limits, prepaid top-up and usage warnings; QM admission check of rolling-window spend per person and org. Teams: a disclaimer label per agent message, citation chips that open the source, feedback {thumb, reason: not asked|inaccurate|low quality|too slow, comment}, explicit allow/block per agent app with reasons. Grok Bot: closed vocabulary of system-event kinds covering every resume path, typed result unions per tool, first-token and idle deadlines with server-paced retry. Buzz evals: task containers run the real product process tree with a roster manifest, scripted human actors, assertions on thread placement, notifications and silence plus an LLM judge, used as release regression.

title: Persistent per-agent computer with lifecycle UX and a governed egress boundary
summary: Grow the credential-free, network-less, run-scoped code_interpreter workspace into a per-(Space, agent) computer: a resource record with lifecycle states (absent, hibernated, starting, running), a durable home that survives runs, hibernate and pre-thaw on presence intent, and a room view of its files and processes with stop/kill. Route its network through Quarry with per-turn capability tokens and an audience egress floor (intersection of allowed hosts, union of denied), and add pattern-triggered process watches. Design the execute target so the user's own machine can be added later.
whyItMatters: An agent that works like a colleague with its own PC is the other half of the Grok Bot vision. Today the sandbox is deliberately hermetic, so agents cannot reach anything, and inline runs lose their edits, so there is no durable workplace to show in the room.

others: buzz (agents as supervised local processes, pluggable computer backends)

title: Room content hardening: read authorization for attachments and transcripts, stricter CSP, anti-spoofing, link and download safety
summary: Four small web changes for a UI that renders other people's and agents' content. Check room membership and audience on attachment and transcript reads and render an explicit 'restricted' state instead of swallowing the 403. Tighten the CSP (Trusted Types with a sanitiser policy, narrower connect-src and img-src, report-only candidate policy with a report endpoint, subresource integrity). Keep agent-generated HTML in the sandboxed no-network iframe and approval UI in the main origin. Mark agent-sourced links and files and serve attachments with safe headers.
whyItMatters: An XSS or exfiltration channel in a room acts with a user's agent authority. Several cheap controls already exist; these changes close the remaining broad allowances (img-src and connect-src allow any https host) and the silent 403.

others: buzz (kind-level read policy; attachment ACL gap to avoid)
slack (link, protocol and download safety)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Strict CSP with Trusted Types: 2 of 5 (teams, slack); fine-grained read authz: 1 of 5 (buzz); trusted sensitive UI: 1 of 5 (teams); link and download safety: 1 of 5 (slack).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: CSP: default-src 'self', nonce-based script-src, require-trusted-types-for 'script' with named policies, object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', plus a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only with a stricter candidate and SRI integrity for every build chunk. Reads: a kind-level policy consulted on every read path (query, push, search) returns not-found for hidden kinds, and attachment reads check the parent message's room ACL. Links: scheme allowlist, warnings for unusual protocols, safe download headers.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: The server gate is right but the UI hides it; attachment authorization per room is not recorded; the CSP lets agent- or member-authored markdown trigger requests to arbitrary https hosts (images, fetch), which is a known exfiltration channel (inference); no Trusted Types or SRI.

approachOriginal: Frontend Plane gateway: confirm attachment fetches check room membership and audience and add not-found semantics for hidden kinds; Frontend: render a restricted state for 403. nginx.conf: add require-trusted-types-for with a DOMPurify policy, replace connect-src https: with the own API and the telemetry host, restrict img-src to own origin plus a media proxy for chat images, add a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only candidate and a gateway report endpoint, add an SRI plugin to the Vite build. Keep approval dialogs in the main origin and agent HTML only in sandbox-html iframes. Mark agent-sourced links, allow only https and mailto without a warning, and serve attachments with Content-Disposition attachment and nosniff.
risks: Third-party scripts (Turnstile, Nexi checkout) can break under Trusted Types. Remote chat-media images need a proxy. Over-tight CSP can break existing embeds, so roll out through report-only first.

verevon.exactGap: The server side is already deny-by-default: room transcript, thread list, activity, knowledge and work reads all take a Control shared-read decision and the transcript route returns 403 space_read_not_authorized (spaces.rs:2616-2680), but SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:201 swallows that 403 with .catch(() => null) and falls back to the thread preview, and a declined read leaves the thread list owner-bound (spaces.rs:1158-1165), so a room whose org has not enabled shared reads silently shows only your own posts as previews. nginx.conf:70 enforces a CSP with connect-src 'self' https:, img-src 'self' data: https: blob: and style-src 'unsafe-inline' and has no Trusted Types, report-only policy or report endpoint, and the markdown renderer builds [text](url) anchors with no scheme or destination check (chat-media-markdown.tsx:1278-1279), though script-src 'self' without unsafe-inline already blocks javascript: execution. Spaces have no attachments or download route to protect (chat documents upload is user-scoped, documents.rs:54), so a per-room attachment ACL is moot until attachments ship.
reuse: The existing Control shared-read decision on every Space read route (shared_thread_read_decision) as the single authorization point; add attachments to it rather than a parallel check
sandbox-html.ts preview CSP plus sandbox="allow-scripts" without allow-same-origin for any agent HTML
Mermaid securityLevel strict and KaTeX trust false, which already close the few innerHTML sinks (only three exist in src)
nginx.conf CSP variable and its per-location re-emit pattern for adding a Report-Only header
Gateway nosniff header (main.rs:157) for download responses
verevon.constraints: Authorization stays with Control and the owning plane through the gateway; the restricted state is a UI rendering of the existing 403 and must not leak anything the read decision withheld (the preview fallback is only safe because the declined listing is owner-bound). The 403 is a per-room or per-org policy outcome, not a per-post one, so it is one room-level message. Tightening connect-src and img-src is a Frontend Plane nginx change, but connect-src https: is deliberately broad for Nexi and telemetry and img-src https: serves web-search thumbnails, favicons and remote chat media (nginx.conf:46-70, DashboardSearchResults.tsx), so narrowing needs a host inventory and a media proxy and must roll out Report-Only first. Third-party Turnstile and Nexi scripts can break under Trusted Types. Attachment read checks belong to the future Space attachment contract (Data Plane document with a Space-bound grant), not to this item.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Re-scope to what is real. (1) S: render a room-level 'restricted' state when the transcript or thread read is refused, instead of silently showing previews. (2) S: add a scheme allowlist (https and mailto) and show the destination host for external markdown links, which also covers link-text spoofing; javascript: is already blocked by script-src but defense in depth is cheap, and the more important need grows once human posts render through ChatMarkdown (F-t1-032). (3) M: a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only candidate with a gateway report endpoint, then narrow connect-src and img-src behind a media proxy. Demote Trusted Types (three innerHTML sinks, all already sanitized, and DOMPurify is not a direct dependency) and drop SRI (script-src is 'self' on same-origin hashed assets, so SRI adds little). Remove the standalone attachment-ACL work and attach it to the attachments feature.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged in size but re-scoped: restricted state and link rules are S, the CSP report-only rollout is the M part; Trusted Types and SRI are removed or demoted.
verevon.verdictReason: The deny-by-default server gate and the sandboxed agent-HTML path already exist, so the item should shrink to the swallowed 403, link safety and a report-only CSP rollout, and drop the attachment-ACL, Trusted Types and SRI work.

title: Org audit trail for admins: role-gated view, Space decisions and agent invocations, SIEM export, usage ledger export
summary: Expose audit-core to org admins and auditors through a role-gated, cursor-paginated API and view, and an export token that streams or pulls events (metadata only). Record signed Space decisions (decision id, subject, audience revision, agent principal, privacy tier, outcome), agent invocations, approvals and moderation actions. Add per-Space and per-agent attribution and a bounded export window to the usage ledger for finance.
whyItMatters: Enterprises that adopt an agent workspace must answer which agent did what, on whose authority. Verevon already signs decisions, so exporting them is cheap and differentiating. The current read path also looks too broad: any authenticated org member can list the org's events.

others: qm (source-level mechanics: recordOnce idempotency, audited admin reads, spend ledger and bounded export)
teams (Purview audit)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: SIEM-grade audit: 2 of 5 (slack DOC, qm SRC); spend export: 1 of 5 (qm). Differentiator.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Append-only table keyed by org and sequence with a unique idempotency key; fire-and-forget record() and exactly-once recordOnce(key); a read API filters by scope, action and time with cursor pagination; an org-admin token streams JSON events (actor, action, entity, context, details, app) to a SIEM; message bodies are never logged; each export is itself audited. Spend: a ledger by day, scope, origin and model with a bounded, token-authenticated export.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: The audit and usage pipes exist, but there is no admin-scoped audit view or export, no cursor, no Space, agent or decision-id dimension, and decisions are not recorded. The read handler appears to rely on org binding alone, so a normal member could read all org events (needs a trace through audit-core to confirm).

approachOriginal: audit-core: add cursor pagination, filters for plane, subject, resource_id, outcome and decision_id, require an admin or auditor role from the signed delegation (self-scope for ordinary members), and per-org export tokens with audited exports. Control user-core: emit space.decision.issued and space.decision.denied events (metadata only). Model Plane: session-core audit_publisher already records tool actions with data category and zdr; add agent-invocation and approval events. cost-core and session-core add space_ref and agent principal to usage metadata. Gateway: /api/v1/admin/audit and an export route. Frontend: an admin Audit view filterable by Space, agent and decision id. Under ZDR carry metadata only. First step in W1: trace the audit-core read handler; if a normal member can read all org events, fix that as a bug before building the admin view.
dependencies: Control decision ids on every effect
planeOwner: Control Plane (audit-core) with Frontend Plane gateway
risks: An export is a mass exfiltration path, so reads must be audited and scoped. Event volume. The tool_action consumer in the Trust Center must keep working when the read path is role-gated.

verevon.exactGap: audit-core already ingests JetStream events (session-core tool_action and tool_action_reserved, user-core erasure and dsar_export through a durable outbox, leads-core, conversation-core, ingestion) and serves GET /v1/audit and /v1/usage(/summary) with org, since, until, event and user_id filters (limit default 100, no cursor) plus a daily retention purge. The access concern is CONFIRMED by trace (SRC): the gateway list_audit only needs a session and forwards the filters, audit-core verifies that the signed delegation binds the org but never consults the delegated role, so any org member can read all org events including other users via user_id; the settings "Recent security events" panel is described as admin review material but is not gated. Missing: admin or auditor gating, cursor pagination, plane/subject/resource filters, export, Space decision and agent-invocation events (user-core decision issuance emits nothing and decisions are stateless signed tokens), and Space or agent dimensions on the usage ledger (cost-core Entry carries org, user, producer, run and model only).

verevon.constraints: audit-core enforces subject, plane and producer authority (subscriber.go:287-295), so each plane must emit its own events: Space decisions from user-core under verevon.audit.v2.control.user-core.*, agent invocations from session-core under verevon.audit.v2.model.session-core.*; Model-side subjects also need nats-provisioner manifest entries (SRC audit_publisher.rs:28-36). Metadata only: audit details JSONB must never hold message content or the decision token (ZDR); tool_action already carries data_category and zdr. Decisions are issued per effect, so persisting every decision is high volume (INF): record denials and effect-bound decisions with decision_ref, not every read decision. The admin role must come from the signed delegation claim (UserRole is already carried and verified but unused). A role-gated read path must not break the Trust Center tool_action aggregation, so keep a self-scoped member view. An export is a mass-exfiltration path and must itself be audited, bounded and token-scoped. Org retention for audit is a single global AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS; per-org values (org_compliance.audit_log_retention_days) are dormant (see F-t1-051).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split out the access-control defect as an S security fix and ship it first: gateway requires admin or owner for org-wide reads, audit-core honors claims.UserRole and forces user_id to the caller for non-admins, and the settings panel is gated with the existing workspace-admin check. Then build cursor pagination, filters and the export token. For decisions, emit from user-core through its existing durable audit outbox, for denials and effect-bound decisions only. For agent invocations reuse session-core audit or run-lifecycle events. Add space_ref and agent_ref to cost-core usage entries through the producer, not by reading another plane database.
verevon.effortNote: M overall as written; the role-gating fix is S and should be tracked as its own W1 security item.
verevon.verdictReason: The suspected read-path defect is confirmed by trace and should lead the item; and "exporting signed decisions is cheap" is wrong because decisions are not recorded anywhere today, so emission must be built.

title: Composer for real work: rich text, persistent drafts, queue and steer while a turn runs, attachments and paste chips, scheduled send, and ref-based context chips with a pre-send preview
summary: Replace the plain textarea with a rich-text composer that emits markdown plus mention refs, render human posts through the same ChatMarkdown as agent output, keep per-room and per-thread drafts across navigation and failed sends, wire the existing queue and steer backend into the Space composer, and add attachments (including folder drop), long-paste chips, model presets and scheduled send. Add 'Ask the agent about this' from canvas, list, file, artifact and Work/Knowledge/Activity selections: the selection travels as a typed reference chip, the exact payload is shown before sending, and the Model Plane frames it as quoted, capped, untrusted data.
whyItMatters: The composer is where people and agents meet; today it is a disabled-while-sending textarea whose text is lost on navigation, and human posts render as plain text while agent posts get full markdown. Buzz's context hand-off shows how to give an agent context without copying content into the transcript.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-08] grokbot: Tiptap/ProseMirror with a restricted schema (paragraph, lists, code, link, mention chip) serialised to markdown on send, Shift+Enter as a user setting, dir=auto per paragraph. buzz: draft keyed by (room, thread) holding text, mentions, attachment refs and a revision; clearing writes an empty tombstone with a higher revision so late async completions cannot resurrect it. grokbot send pipeline: client nonce, local journal, server dedupes by message id, bubble confirms on transcript echo, typed delivery ACCEPTED|DUPLICATE|REFUSED and an UNKNOWN_DURABILITY state. qm: editable queue chips while a run streams and a steer promotion through a durable RunSignal. title: SPA realtime client layer: client-supplied idempotency key, send states with in-place optimistic row, normalized store with version guards, offline vs service-down banner
summary: Make the composer generate an idempotency_key per send and reuse it on retry (a new key only when the content changes), expose queued, sending, accepted and failed states, and key the timeline row by that key until the canonical id arrives from the stream, reconciling in place. Replace per-component fetches with a Solid store keyed by entity id that stream frames and fetches patch with version guards (a write supersedes an older in-flight read). Add a connectivity service that probes a no-auth gateway health route to tell offline from service-down and shows a banner with the last-fresh time.
whyItMatters: The gateway generates its own idempotency key when the composer omits one, so a client retry after a timeout creates a second append and a second billed AI turn. A store that push frames can patch is needed to apply the stream cleanly, and the room should explain unreachable states instead of showing stale data. These are small, cheap changes with direct cost and trust payoff.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (send journal with stages queued, prepared, dispatching, accepted-awaiting-echo; resource state machine with stale-while-revalidate and write-supersedes-read guards); Slack for connectivity states
others: Buzz (content-addressed event ids with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; optimistic-<uuid> row swapped on success keeping the render key)
QM (idempotency keys and 5-minute replay window at every ingress)
Teams (central data layer with normalized cache; DOC/SRC)
Slack (online, slackDown, offline via unauthenticated api.test probe; sleep and wake forwarded)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Client generates a send id on Enter and persists it with the draft; server insert is ON CONFLICT (tenant, send_id) DO NOTHING and returns was_inserted; the client marks accepted only when the echo with the same send id arrives. Resource<T> = {state: loading, ready, failed(prev), empty, unavailable, value, version}. Probe a cheap no-auth health endpoint on connection errors, listen to online/offline, visibilitychange and page freeze/resume, and resync on resume.

approachOriginal: Composer (SpaceRoomComposer.tsx): generate the key per send, store it with the pending exchange, send it in the append body so spaces.rs passes it into the Control thread:append decision; confirm Session Core dedupes on (thread, key) and returns the existing turn, otherwise add it in append_message_in_tx. Connectivity: small service using the existing gateway unauthenticated /health route (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/main.rs:91, rate-limit exempt) as the probe plus online/offline, visibilitychange and freeze/resume hooks feeding the watchdog of F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-01) and a room banner. Coordinate with F-t1-032 (R-t1-01-08) (composer states and queueing).

risks: Content-bound decisions: a retry with edited content must get a new key. Store refactor churn across SpacePage components. Gateway health probe must stay unauthenticated and content-free.

verevon.exactGap: The gateway already honors a client-supplied idempotency_key for Space thread create and append (spaces.rs required_or_generated at :136 and :192; the key is not in FORGED_SPACE_AUTHORITY_FIELDS) and Control binds it into the decision digest, but the composer never sends one and nothing dedupes (SRC): Control decisions are stateless signed tokens, and Session Core append_message_in_tx assigns a fresh ULID and derives the event idempotency hash from message id and sequence, not from the client key. The composer sends through the SSE POST /api/v1/chat/stream with one in-flight exchange (streaming, done, stopped, error), blocks while submitting and does not use the existing resumeStream/resume route that the main chat controller uses; the timeline is a 6 s poll with a latestThreadRequest ordering guard and a module-level published store (space-live-work.ts), and there is no offline versus service-down banner, only a threadsUnavailable flag. verevon.verdictReason: Core idea is right and cheap, but the dependency "verify Session Core dedupes" resolves negatively (it does not), the owning plane includes Model, and the normalized-store part is optional given existing guards.

title: Scalable room timeline: server-computed windows with exact cursors and reply summaries, virtualised rows with scroll anchoring, jump-to-latest and history paging
summary: Add a Session Core query and gateway route that returns windows of top-level threads with reply count, last reply time and participants kept at write time, a keyset cursor on server seq and id and a limit+1 has_more probe. Window the SpaceRoomTimeline rows with a pure, tested anchoring policy (hold the anchor on prepend, auto-scroll on append only while pinned to the bottom, otherwise show Jump to latest), page older turns on scroll, support jump to thread or date, and keep aria-setsize/posinset.
whyItMatters: Every 6 s poll reloads the full thread list and then fetches each transcript (N+1); with push and streaming the view will jump. Buzz's cursor windows and anchoring policy are the tested pattern.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz (NIP-CW timeline windows: top_level, include_summaries, composite until + before_id cursor, thread_metadata computed at ingest); Buzz (written, tested anchoring policy on a patched virtual list, mobile IME handling)

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-09-07] 1 of 5; unique [R-t1-12-06] 2 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-09-07] Maintain thread_metadata (reply_count, last_reply_at, participants) at write time; page with WHERE (created_at, id) < (until, before_id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT n+1 and return summaries inline; reject client timestamps beyond a skew bound or order by server seq instead so keyset order is replica-safe. [R-t1-12-06] Virtual list with measured row heights; anchoring state {pinnedToBottom, anchorRowId, anchorOffset}: on prepend preserve anchor offset, on append scroll only if pinned, show Jump-to-latest when not pinned and new rows arrive; ResizeObserver plus FLIP animates siblings when a row grows, disabled under reduced motion.

[R-t1-12-06] No virtualisation, no scroll anchoring and no paging: the full thread list loads on every 6 s poll, so the view will jump once realtime or streaming lands.

[R-t1-12-06] Frontend Plane: a windowing layer for the timeline with a standalone anchoring-policy module and lifecycle tests, plus a turn-paged history call from Model Plane through the gateway. Because the app is on Solid 2.0 RC with no virtual-list dependency, first confirm that @tanstack/solid-virtual works on Solid 2, otherwise implement windowing with IntersectionObserver and measured heights.

[R-t1-12-06] Virtualisation breaks find-in-page and screen-reader reading order unless handled; Solid 2 RC compatibility of third-party list libraries; unmeasured rows cause scroll jumps.

A room 'reply' is a turn inside the thread and normalizeTranscriptTurns keeps only the first 30 turns (MAX_TURNS_PER_POST), so the newest turns of a long post are silently dropped; session-core has no reply_count, last_reply or participant fields.

Cursors must carry no authority: every page re-runs the Control shared read decision and the audience-revision ceiling already applied in list_threads, and summary participants must be filtered per reader so a reply count cannot leak a thread the reader may not see. Keyset order needs a persisted sort key: the current order is computed at read time from the last message, so a (pinned, last_activity_at, id) cursor needs a stored last_activity_at (or message sequence) column plus an index, not a derived expression. ZDR threads are persistence-free and never appear in the listing.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Ship the client-only slice first (S): fix the first-30 truncation by paging the transcript from the newest turn backwards, add jump-to-latest and pinned-to-bottom anchoring on poll using the chat precedent and a pure tested policy module, keep aria-setsize/posinset, and try content-visibility/IntersectionObserver per the UI audit before adding a virtual-list dependency (verify solid-virtual on Solid 2 RC only if needed). Then the server slice (M): migration adding a persisted last_activity_at and turn_count/last_turn_at/participant ids maintained at append time, a before/limit+1 has_more query in Session Core, a gateway route with before/limit, and lazy transcript fetch per visible post. Treat 'reply summaries' as per-thread turn summaries, since replies are turns in the post, and drop the dependency on F-t1-003 server seq unless it ships first.

title: Attention outside the open tab: installable PWA, content-free Web Push with service-worker Open/Reply, in-tab toasts, tab-title and app badge
summary: Add a web app manifest, a versioned service worker (build-id-keyed shell cache, reconnecting page, push and notificationclick handlers) and an install affordance. Add Web Push (VAPID) subscriptions per device in notification-core where the push payload is only an opaque wake plus a notification id; the service worker fetches the notification through the gateway and renders it, honouring hide-preview, with Open and Reply only (an approval opens the approval view, never approves from a toast). In the tab, add one toast store fed by the attention stream, a tab-title and favicon count and navigator.setAppBadge from the unread map with a monotonic projection, and optional per-signal sounds.
whyItMatters: There is no manifest, service worker or push, so an agent that finishes or needs approval while the tab is closed cannot reach anyone. Buzz's content-free wake push is the reference pattern that fits ZDR; the native desktop shell (5 of 5 references) can come later on top of this.

teams (presence-aware tray icon, jump list)
grokbot (monotonic unread projection feeding the badge)
Slack (grouped toasts, reply input, content-free logs)

Grok Bot (permission state reported to the server, active-device routing)
Slack (HTML toast window, 13-14 named sounds, tray and overlay cues)

Presence outside the open tab is treated as table stakes by every native client. [R-t1-05-05] 4 of 5 sources across push, native toasts and permission handling; common [R-t1-05-08] 4 of 5 sources; toasts common, badge and sounds table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-11-01] One web build with a shared breakpoint constant for CSS and JS and a visualViewport listener to keep the composer above the keyboard (qm); web manifest plus service worker for app shell and Web Push; Badging API fed by an aggregated unread count; Slack derives a three-state icon (rest/unread/highlight) plus a count tooltip from the same aggregate. [R-t1-05-05] Buzz: the device registers an encrypted, expiring (at most 30 days), installation-scoped lease with self-only filters; after read-authorization checks the server queues a wake; a blind gateway sends a constant payload; the client wakes, fetches pending items through the authenticated API, verifies and renders locally, so neither the push provider nor the gateway sees content. Slack builds a ToastGeneric toast from the normalised payload with grouped header, avatar, reply input and action buttons; the reply dispatches with channel, thread and trace ids and logs only non-content fields. Grok Bot reports {platform, os_permission, can_ask_again, in_app_enabled} per device so the server skips denied devices; Slack throttles macOS re-prompts (3 per session, 10 minutes apart). On the web the equivalent is showNotification with actions plus a notificationclick handler. [R-t1-05-08] Teams draws its own toast panel (corner, compact or comfortable density, grouped collections, in-place update) and a separate web-layer banner system, distinguishing in-context banners from OS toasts. Grok Bot computes the badge from the same roster as the sidebar, skips muted or hidden items, and rejects stale snapshots by epoch and sequence so the number never moves backwards. Slack stores a sound id per event type and plays it in the web layer when visible, otherwise passes it to the OS notification.
